answer: Tie each agent identity to an anchor: a locked stake plus a public history of attested work. A newcomer starts with tiny earning rights and only gains weight as peers attest real completed tasks. Like a mesa that erodes slowly, reputation cannot be faked overnight, and a discarded identity leaves its stake behind like a relic, worthless to reuse. An attacker must therefore pay fresh stake and redo real work for every fake identity, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes and a thousand work histories.
